summary: Round 3 fresh review of all 9 units. The three requested fixes are present and consistent. (1) Cervical screening: the fixed 3 and 5 year intervals are gone, replaced by the hedged 'recall intervals depend on the HPV result and have been changing (3 to 5 years); follow the current NHS Cervical Screening Programme policy' wording, and no question key, worked example or marking guide depends on a recall interval (q003 and the worked example use only the 12-month repeat after hrHPV positive with normal cytology, which is standard). (2) PID: the pelvic-pain unit now reads as a single IM ceftriaxone dose with doxycycline and metronidazole for 14 days, matching the sexual-health unit and BASHH-style practice. (3) Ulipristal extra-precaution wording and the Abortion Act hedging (lesson, summary and q008 stem) are present. All numeric keys were recomputed and are correct (BMI 16.4, fibroid volume 73.3, PPV 19.6, RMI 3,060 and 450, discordance 25, MMR 73.1 and 80/48.4/39.5 percent, shock index 1.28, Pearl 2, cumulative 24.6, progesterone day 25, TMSC 28.8, fold change 8, 114 true positives); MCQ keys, FIGO 2018, Quintero, RMI, UKMEC, steroid, magnesium and eclampsia content all check out. No critical or major issues remain; only five minor points, one of which is hedged but unverifiable. This is an AI review: the course still needs a subject-matter expert (clinician) before clinical reliance, and all regimens, thresholds, legal statements and screening intervals should be checked against current NICE, FSRH, BASHH, NHS England, RCOG and UK law sources.

issues.problem: The screening paragraph now repeats the identical parenthetical twice ('recall intervals depend on the HPV result and have been changing (3 to 5 years); follow the current NHS Cervical Screening Programme policy'), once after 'women aged 25 to 64 are invited' and again after 'routine recall'. The text is safe but reads as an editing artefact, and 'depend on the HPV result' does not tell the student what the current interval for a negative result is. Whether the current England interval is 5 years for hrHPV-negative women aged 25 to 49 is unverified here.
issues.suggestedFix: State the hedge once, after 'routine recall', and (after a source check of current NHS England policy) optionally add the current interval for hrHPV-negative women. Keep the instruction to follow current NHSCSP policy and keep all questions interval-free.

issues.problem: FIGO 2018 size boundaries are written as 'IB1 ... up to 2 cm', 'IB2 = more than 2 cm and up to 4 cm', 'IB3 ... over 4 cm' (table and worked example). FIGO 2018 defines IB1 as less than 2 cm, IB2 as 2 cm or more but less than 4 cm, and IB3 as 4 cm or more, so a tumour of exactly 2 cm or 4 cm is mis-staged by the wording. No question key is affected (2.6 cm and 5 cm).
issues.suggestedFix: Reword to IB1 less than 2 cm, IB2 2 cm or more and less than 4 cm, IB3 4 cm or more, in the table and the worked example (check against the FIGO 2018 source).

issues.problem: The investigation list says 'a high FSH means ovarian failure; a low or normal FSH means the hypothalamus or pituitary'. A normal FSH is also found in PCOS, outflow tract obstruction, Asherman syndrome and androgen insensitivity or MRKH, so the rule is oversimplified and could mislead a student away from structural causes.
issues.suggestedFix: Say: a high FSH points to ovarian failure; a low or normal FSH with low oestradiol points to hypothalamic or pituitary causes, but normal FSH is also found in PCOS and in structural or outflow tract disorders, so interpret with examination and imaging.

issues.problem: The patient is 17 and the marking guide asks the student to 'Assess capacity and understanding (Gillick competence)'. Gillick competence applies to children under 16; in England 16 and 17 year olds are presumed to have capacity to consent to treatment (and the Mental Capacity Act applies), and Scotland uses separate legislation. The safeguarding point about the 29-year-old partner and the confidentiality advice are sound.
issues.suggestedFix: Change to: a 16 or 17 year old is presumed to have capacity (assess if in doubt); Gillick competence applies under 16. Keep the age-difference safeguarding assessment and the limits of confidentiality.

issues.problem: Unverified or loosely scoped legal content: the lesson applies Gillick competence to termination of pregnancy in a unit that also says the Abortion Act covers Scotland, but Gillick is an English and Welsh doctrine (Scotland uses the Age of Legal Capacity (Scotland) Act 1991). Two-doctor certification and Ground C are hedged ('check current law') but recent reforms to criminal liability and remote early medical abortion are not mentioned, and I cannot verify their current status.
issues.suggestedFix: Add 'in England and Wales (Scotland and Northern Ireland differ)' when citing Gillick, and recommend a source check of the current Abortion Act position, keeping the existing 'check current law' wording in the lesson, summary and q008.
